question.text: The velocity of upper layer of water in a river is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Shearing stress between horizontal layers of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Depth of the river is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. (Co-efficient of viscosity of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>)

solution.text:
The viscous force formula is given by,

F=-ηAdvdy

Therefore, shear stress FA=-ηdvdy. Here negative sign tells us that the direction of force is opposite to the velocity gradient.

⇒FA=ηdvdy

Now v=36×518=10 m s-1 and if the depth is d

dvdy=10d

⇒10-3=10-2×10d⇒d=100 m
